# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is a personal book on machine learning. It starts with the linear algebra behind a dot product and ends with how large language models are trained, aligned, served, and evaluated. It also covers what an interviewer expects you to explain on a whiteboard.

Each chapter does four things:

1. **Explains** the idea, intuition first and then the full derivation, with no steps skipped.
2. **Builds** the idea from scratch in NumPy (or PyTorch) and **checks** the result against a library. All code in this book runs when the book is built.
3. **Works examples** by hand and in code, at least two for each major idea.
4. **Tests** you with graded exercises that have collapsible solutions, followed by interview questions with model answers.

## Map of the book

Five volumes, sixteen parts, 155 chapters (Vol 1: 16 · Vol 2: 39 · Vol 3: 42 · Vol 4: 40 · Vol 5: 18), plus the two CS249r *Machine Learning Systems* volumes bundled in Part XV. Each part depends only on the parts before it. This is a comprehensive guide: each chapter runs about 25–60 pages, with full derivations, at least 15 exercises, and at least 12 interview questions.

| Volume | Part | Topic | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · Foundations** | I | Tools | NumPy, pandas and EDA, PyTorch |
| | II | Mathematics | Linear algebra, matrix calculus, probability, the Gaussian, inference, Bayesian inference, convex analysis, optimization, information theory, numerical computation |
| **2 · Classical ML** | III | Supervised learning | The learning problem, linear and logistic regression, regularization, perceptron, generative classifiers, k-NN, kernels, SVMs, trees, forests, boosting, GPs |
| | IV | ML in practice | End-to-end projects, features, metrics, validation, imbalance, calibration and conformal prediction, A/B tests, interpretability, learning with few labels |
| | V | Unsupervised and probabilistic models | Clustering, GMM/EM, PCA/ICA/FA, manifold learning, anomaly detection, graphical models, HMMs and Kalman filters, MCMC, variational inference |
| | VI | Learning theory | PAC and VC, Rademacher complexity and stability, online learning |
| **3 · Deep Learning** | VII | Deep learning foundations | MLPs, autograd, losses, initialization, optimizers, normalization, regularization, residual nets, training recipe, generalization, transfer, representation learning |
| | VIII | Computer vision | Classical vision, convolutions, CNNs, detection, segmentation, ViT, self-supervised learning and CLIP, video, 3D |
| | IX | NLP and sequence models | Classical NLP, embeddings, sequence labelling, RNNs, seq2seq, the Transformer, BERT/GPT/T5, GPT from scratch, decoding |
| | X | Generative models | Autoregressive models, VAEs, GANs, flows, EBMs and score matching, diffusion, flow matching, latent diffusion, evaluation |
| **4 · RL, LLMs and Agents** | XI | Reinforcement learning | Bandits, MDPs, TD, DQN, policy gradients, PPO/SAC, model-based RL, imitation learning, offline RL |
| | XII | Large language models | Tokenization, pretraining and scaling, architecture, efficient attention, MoE, SSMs, PEFT, alignment, reasoning, inference, RAG, multimodal models, evaluation, interpretability |
| | XIII | Agentic systems | Workflows vs agents, context engineering, tool use and MCP, planning, memory, harnesses, multi-agent systems, coding and computer-use agents, evaluation, training, security, operations |
| **5 · Applications and Career** | XIV | Specialized topics | Recommenders, learning to rank, time series, GNNs, causal inference, speech and audio |
| | XV | ML systems | **CS249r Vol 1 and 2 bundled** (PDF/EPUB), with chapter-by-chapter guides. CS249r Vol 3 and 4 will be plugged in when released |
| | XVI | Interview preparation | ML system design cases, coding drills, question bank, probability puzzles |

Parts are added as they are written. The full outline is in `PLAN.md`.

## Prerequisites

High-school algebra and basic Python. Part I covers the tools and Part II builds the rest of the mathematics the book needs.
